{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABXS3DBw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhA2q5c", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 9, "title": "Fix LoRA padding-loss masking and validate it with a controlled MBPP experiment", "body": "## Problem

The original 100-step LoRA adapter for Qwen3-4B performed worse than its base model on the same 500 MBPP test tasks:

| Metric | Base | Original 100-step LoRA |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pass@1 | 358/500 (71.6%) | 338/500 (67.6%) |

Of 500 tasks, 16 changed from fail to pass while 36 changed from pass to fail. All 36 regressions were reproduced. Their analysis reported 25 logic/value mistakes, 7 syntax errors, 3 argument/type/index errors, and 1 floating-point exact-comparison case. A smaller 20-example validation check instead improved from 90% to 95%, failing to reveal the broader regression. Investigation also reported that **padding tokens may contribute to the training loss**, but the impact on accuracy is unproven.

The current project delegates training to pinned `mlx-lm==0.32.0` via `scripts/experiment.py` and selects just 20 validation examples from official MBPP training IDs 601–974. We need to verify/correct any unintended PAD-token loss and design a more reliable, leakage-free validation process *without conflating the PAD fix with changes to the training set*.

## Expected outcome

Make training-loss masking correct and verifiable, enlarge or strengthen validation using only permitted MBPP training IDs, and provide a **controlled experiment comparing identical LoRA training runs with and without the padding-loss correction**. The comparison must isolate the masking change and report whether it affects correctness, rather than assuming the discovered issue explains the -4 percentage-point result.

## Context

- Repository: `takahirox/llm-finetuning`, branch `main`. Existing training uses `scripts.experiment train`, `mlx_lm lora`, pinned configuration in `configs/experiment.json`, and an immutable model revision.
- The existing data split uses 354 train + 20 loss-validation tasks (IDs 601–974), with official MBPP test IDs 11–510 evaluated separately.
- The prior 500-task test results (71.6% vs 67.6%) have already been examined. **Do not repeatedly tune to this test set**. Treat it as previously observed evidence; use a clean validation split for development and consider an independent final holdout for generalization claims.
- Existing adapters and reports are historical artifacts: do not overwrite them or imply that a new split makes their scores a controlled baseline.
- Follow [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). New collaboration material must be in English.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Diagnose and correct training-loss masking
- [ ] Inspect the exact installed/pinned MLX-LM dataset collator and loss computation, including prompt masking, padding, truncation and any EOS/PAD token-ID overlap. Reproduce the reported PAD-loss behavior with a minimal deterministic example; document whether and where it occurs.
- [ ] Ensure **only intended target/completion tokens** contribute to the LoRA objective: padding and masked prompt positions must not contribute. Establish this with token-level label/loss-mask assertions (including mixed-length batches, truncated examples, and EOS/PAD overlap if applicable), not just an aggregate training-loss check.
- [ ] Implement the smallest maintainable fix in the project integration or via a verified upstream dependency change; do not silently patch files inside a developer's virtual environment. Pin and record changed dependencies/behavior as needed. If an upstream-compatible correction cannot be made safely, fail explicitly and document the blocking reason instead of claiming success.
- [ ] Guard against a regression with automated tests. Verify that normal non-padding completion tokens still receive loss and that the change does not inadvertently alter prompt masking.

### Improve validation without leaking test data
- [ ] Support a documented, deterministic **larger internal validation split** (e.g. 80 of MBPP IDs 601–974) using seed and task-ID manifests/hashes; never select official test IDs 11–510 for training or validation. Confirm disjoint train/validation/test IDs and no reference-solution leakage.
- [ ] Document the reduced training-set size that comes with enlarging validation. Explain why comparing a new 80-validation run directly against the **old 354-train/20-validation adapter** would confound the PAD effect.
- [ ] Provide a meaningful validation readout on more than training loss alone, such as pass@1 with the existing bounded Docker scorer, using fixed held-out validation prompts and identical decoding/scoring conditions for the A/B runs. Preserve provenance and per-task outcomes.

### Controlled A/B experiment
- [ ] Provide documented runnable steps/configurations to train **two fresh LoRA adapters from the same pinned base weights**, using exactly the same enlarged validation split, training IDs/order, seed, 100 iterations, batch size, learning rate, LoRA architecture and remaining settings. The only intentional difference must be **legacy vs corrected PAD-loss masking**. Clearly label the legacy arm as diagnostic and do not make faulty training the normal default.
- [ ] Record/verify the mask variant and dataset/model/code/dependency versions in each adapter's metadata. Use separate ignored output directories and preserve the old adapter/results.
- [ ] Evaluate both A/B adapters on the **same validation examples** and report pass@1, number of successes, signed difference, all four paired transition counts, and any failure/format categories available. Confirm whether the mask difference is reflected in the actual trainer rather than merely a wrapper flag.
- [ ] Avoid claiming that any improvement was caused by the fix unless the mask-only controlled comparison supports it; accurately distinguish regression diagnosis, validation results, and any optional further test-set evaluation.
- [ ] Add focused automated tests for split invariants, loss-mask behavior, variant selection and provenance, and paired result computation. Run appropriate existing tests/syntax/lockfile/README checks before merge, and clearly report what was not executed.
- [ ] Update README or a concise experimental guide with copy-and-run setup/training/validation/comparison commands on Apple Silicon. Keep model weights, datasets, adapters and large generated result files ignored. Propose an Issue-linked PR against `main` and follow repository review policy.

## Optional validation

- On an available Apple Silicon Mac, run the real two-arm 100-step experiment and record elapsed times, train/validation losses, validation pass@1, output-format failures, and provenance. If no suitable Mac or historical artifacts are accessible to the implementing agent, provide runnable commands and **do not invent measured outcomes**.
- Evaluate chosen final settings **once** on a genuinely independent test set not used in tuning, if one can be sourced/constructed with appropriate controls. The already-inspected 500 MBPP test tasks can be presented as a diagnostic comparison but must not serve as the internal model-selection set.
- Investigate learning rate and number of steps in separate follow-up work only after correcting training integrity and validation.

## Required post-merge verification

None automatically required: merging this change triggers no deployment or benchmark run. Record any real training/evaluation not performed as pending future experimentation rather than completed verification.
